clinicalPearls: Typically affects young adults, with a male predominance, presenting with marked hepatosplenomegaly, systemic symptoms, and cytopenias but characteristically no significant lymphadenopathy
A recognised association exists with chronic immunosuppression, including thiopurine and anti-TNF therapy for inflammatory bowel disease and post-transplant immunosuppression
The neoplastic cell is usually a gamma-delta cytotoxic T-lymphocyte that infiltrates the sinusoids of the spleen, liver, and bone marrow
Typical immunophenotype is CD3 positive, CD56 often positive, CD4 and CD8 frequently negative, with expression of the T-cell receptor gamma-delta chain (a minority are alpha-beta)
Isochromosome 7q is a characteristic cytogenetic abnormality, often with trisomy 8
Bone marrow involvement is almost universal, with an intrasinusoidal pattern that can be subtle and easily overlooked
Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis may complicate the course
reference.pathophysiology: Hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma is an aggressive neoplasm of cytotoxic T-cells, most often of the gamma-delta lineage, which normally reside in splenic red pulp and hepatic sinusoids. The tumour cells home to and expand within the sinusoidal compartments of spleen, liver, and bone marrow rather than forming nodal masses. Chronic antigenic stimulation and prolonged immunosuppression are thought to promote clonal outgrowth, and the recurrent isochromosome 7q with trisomy 8 provides a cytogenetic signature. Progressive sinusoidal infiltration causes organomegaly, hypersplenism, and cytopenias, and immune dysregulation can trigger a haemophagocytic syndrome.
additionalDifferentials: Other peripheral T-cell lymphomas involving spleen and marrow
Hepatosplenic involvement by aggressive B-cell lymphoma or leukaemia
Chronic infection or portal hypertension causing hepatosplenomegaly
Hairy cell leukaemia or other splenomegaly-predominant leukaemias
additionalInvestigations: Bone marrow aspirate and trephine with immunohistochemistry, looking for an intrasinusoidal infiltrate
Immunophenotyping for CD3, CD56, CD4, CD8 and the gamma-delta versus alpha-beta T-cell receptor
Cross-sectional imaging of liver and spleen and assessment for lymphadenopathy
Ferritin, triglycerides, fibrinogen, and marrow review to evaluate for haemophagocytosis
redFlags: Rapidly worsening cytopenias with bleeding or infection risk
Features of haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with fever, hyperferritinaemia, and organ dysfunction
Massive splenomegaly at risk of rupture or causing severe hypersplenism
Fulminant hepatic involvement with rising bilirubin and coagulopathy
reference.prognosis: This is one of the most aggressive T-cell lymphomas, with frequent early relapse after combination chemotherapy and short survival unless consolidated with allogeneic or autologous stem-cell transplantation in eligible patients.
pitfalls: Missing the subtle intrasinusoidal marrow infiltrate on routine staining
Assuming hepatosplenomegaly without lymphadenopathy indicates a benign or infective cause
Not recognising the link with prolonged immunosuppression in inflammatory bowel disease or transplantation
Failing to identify and treat an accompanying haemophagocytic syndrome
references: Swerdlow SH et al. WHO monograph on lymphoid neoplasms
management: Induction with intensive non-CHOP combination chemotherapy, favouring platinum- and cytarabine-based or purine-analogue regimens, as the disease-directed mainstay
Consolidation with allogeneic (or autologous) haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation in responding, eligible patients to improve durable control
Withdraw precipitating immunosuppression such as thiopurines and anti-TNF agents where these are implicated
Supportive care with tumour lysis syndrome prophylaxis, transfusion support for cytopenias, and antimicrobial prophylaxis during neutropenia
Prompt recognition and treatment of associated haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with etoposide-based immunochemotherapy
Consider clinical-trial enrolment given the poor prognosis, with early referral to a transplant centre
Multidisciplinary haemato-oncology management with response assessment and relapse surveillance imaging
